title: Optimizing inference for voice models in production - Philip Kiely, Baseten
talk_summary: A Baseten engineer walks through optimizing a TTS model (Orpheus, a Llama 3.2 3B backbone) with TensorRT-LLM, FP8 quantization, and dynamic batching, then argues that infrastructure and client-code latency often dominate runtime gains.

takeaways.technique: Co-locate pipeline stages to kill network hairpins
takeaways.what_they_do: They keep chained model calls in the same data center and avoid DNS hairpins, because each hop's overhead compounds across a multi-step pipeline.
takeaways.evidence_quote: even things as simple as not having to go off and do a hair pin um at the DNS level and come back
takeaways.numbers: hairpinning alone costs 40-50ms across 4-5 steps, ~10% of SLA

takeaways.technique: Reuse warm sessions instead of reconnecting per request
takeaways.what_they_do: They replace naive per-request clients with a multiprocess pool that shares one session across concurrent requests, since session setup dominates.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you're sharing the you're sharing the session between all of these different requests

takeaways.technique: Profile the whole pipeline, not just the model
takeaways.what_they_do: They profiled and found the TTS implementation was CPU-bound at the audio-decode loop, not GPU-bound, which redirected optimization effort.
takeaways.evidence_quote: our TTS imple implementation with Orpheus is actually in many cases CPUbound

takeaways.technique: Quantize small models to FP8 including KV cache
takeaways.what_they_do: They quantized a 3B model to FP8 (weights and KV cache) on Hopper and got acceptable quality, making it cheaper to serve.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we quantize this model to FP8 pretty successfully ... even when we quantize the KV cache
takeaways.numbers: 16-24 simultaneous streams on half an H100 (MIG)

takeaways.technique: Optimize for the latency floor the task needs, then concurrency
takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of maximizing tokens/sec, they target the minimum rate a real-time stream needs, then optimize time-to-first-output and concurrency to fit more users per GPU.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you only want as many tokens per second as you need for a real-time stream
